bull.b: Wynn has moved from losses into sustained profitability while producing substantial operating and free cash flow. This recovery supports ongoing investment, debt servicing and shareholder returns, although the durability of peak margins remains an important consideration.

Healthy EBITDAR margins across Las Vegas, Boston and Macau demonstrate the value of Wynn’s premium integrated-resort model and geographic diversification. Multiple properties contribute meaningful earnings, reducing reliance on a single operating market and enabling cross-selling across resort amenities.

Approximately $4.0 billion of liquidity gives Wynn resources to fund operations and strategic projects while maintaining capital returns. Continued Macau development and the Al Marjan opening plan also provide avenues to expand non-gaming offerings and future resort capacity.

bear.b: Very high debt combined with negative shareholders’ equity leaves Wynn’s capital structure heavily debt-supported and limits financial flexibility. Interest obligations and refinancing needs can constrain investment choices, reduce resilience during weaker travel or gaming conditions, and amplify execution risk.

The larger Al Marjan budget and substantial remaining equity requirement increase Wynn’s capital demands before the project opens. Funding this development alongside Macau commitments may constrain discretionary cash deployment and heighten sensitivity to construction delays, cost escalation or weaker project returns.

Recent margin compression indicates that revenue growth has not translated consistently into expanding earnings power. Rising property operating costs, including wage increases and premium-service investment, could continue to absorb incremental revenue and make profitability more sensitive to changes in customer mix and gaming results.
